description: Calling the reporting service for a period with zero activations returns a well-formed empty-but-valid funnel structure (no exception).
steps: Call the funnel report for a period with no data
Assert a well-formed empty structure is returned, not an exception

description: Plan-mix distribution percentages sum to 100 (within rounding tolerance of 0.1) across all active plans for a given snapshot.
steps: Seed multiple active plans with subscribers
Call plan_mix report
Assert the percentages sum to 100 within 0.1 tolerance

description: ARPU trend values are clearly labeled as stubbed/synthetic in the returned structure's metadata.
steps: Call the ARPU report
Assert the response metadata includes a stubbed/synthetic label

description: A non-admin principal invoking the service directly (bypassing the API) still receives an authorization error, not just relying on the API layer.
steps: Call the reporting service function directly with a non-admin principal
Assert an authorization error is raised at the service layer

description: GET /api/admin/reports/activation-funnel (admin role) returns HTTP 200 with per-stage counts.
steps: GET the endpoint as admin
Assert response status 200 with per-stage counts

description: GET /api/admin/reports/churn returns HTTP 200 with monthly churn values.
steps: GET the endpoint as admin
Assert response status 200 with monthly churn values

description: GET /api/admin/reports/plan-mix returns HTTP 200 with per-plan percentage distribution.
steps: GET the endpoint as admin
Assert response status 200 with per-plan percentages

description: GET /api/admin/reports/arpu returns HTTP 200 with a stubbed ARPU trend series.
steps: GET the endpoint as admin
Assert response status 200 with a labeled stubbed ARPU series

description: A non-admin principal calling any of the four endpoints receives HTTP 403.
steps: Call each of the four endpoints as a non-admin principal
Assert response status 403 in every case

description: Dashboard renders the activation funnel, churn, plan mix, and ARPU trend using data fetched from the four reporting endpoints.
steps: Load the dashboard
Assert all four panels render with data from their respective endpoints

description: Each panel displays a loading state while its endpoint call is in flight and an error state if the call fails.
steps: Delay/fail one endpoint response
Assert the corresponding panel shows a loading then an error state

description: The plan-mix panel labels each segment with its plan name and percentage.
steps: Load the plan-mix panel with seeded data
Assert each segment shows a plan name and percentage label

description: A CSR or admin can terminate a subscription in state ACTIVE, supplying a reason code, resulting in the subscription transitioning to TERMINATED via the shared FSM.
steps: Set up a subscription in state ACTIVE
Call terminate_subscription() as CSR with a reason code
Assert the subscription becomes TERMINATED

description: A CSR or admin can terminate a subscription in state SUSPENDED, supplying a reason code, resulting in the subscription transitioning to TERMINATED via the shared FSM.
steps: Set up a subscription in state SUSPENDED
Call terminate_subscription() as admin with a reason code
Assert the subscription becomes TERMINATED

description: Terminating a subscription in PENDING_KYC, PORT_OUT_REQUESTED, PORTED_OUT, or TERMINATED raises InvalidSubscriberStateException and writes no StateTransition row.
steps: For each of PENDING_KYC, PORT_OUT_REQUESTED, PORTED_OUT, TERMINATED, set up a subscription in that state
Call terminate_subscription() as CSR with a reason code
Assert InvalidSubscriberStateException is raised and no StateTransition row was written

description: Attempting termination without a reason code is rejected before any state change or StateTransition row is written.
steps: Set up a subscription in state ACTIVE
Call terminate_subscription() with no reason code
Assert rejection and that no state change or StateTransition row was written

description: A non-CSR/non-admin principal (subscriber or dealer-context) attempting termination is rejected.
steps: Call terminate_subscription() as a subscriber principal
Assert an authorization error is raised and no state change occurs

description: A successful termination writes a StateTransition row with a non-null actor, a non-null reason_code, and a timestamp, and logs a structured entry with the masked actor.
steps: Perform a successful termination
Assert the resulting StateTransition row has non-null actor, reason_code, created_at
Capture the emitted log line and assert it is structured JSON with a masked actor

description: POST /api/subscriptions/{id}/terminate on an ACTIVE subscription, called by CSR, returns HTTP 200 with state TERMINATED.
steps: Set up a subscription in state ACTIVE
POST /api/subscriptions/{id}/terminate as CSR with a reason code
Assert response status 200 with state TERMINATED

description: POST /api/subscriptions/{id}/terminate on a SUSPENDED subscription, called by admin, returns HTTP 200 with state TERMINATED.
steps: Set up a subscription in state SUSPENDED
POST /api/subscriptions/{id}/terminate as admin with a reason code
Assert response status 200 with state TERMINATED

description: POST /api/subscriptions/{id}/terminate on a subscription not in ACTIVE/SUSPENDED returns HTTP 409 with reason_code INVALID_STATE_TRANSITION.
steps: Set up a subscription in state PORT_OUT_REQUESTED
POST /api/subscriptions/{id}/terminate as CSR with a reason code
Assert response status 409 with reason_code INVALID_STATE_TRANSITION

description: POST /api/subscriptions/{id}/terminate with a missing reason_code returns HTTP 422 with reason_code VALIDATION_ERROR.
steps: Set up a subscription in state ACTIVE
POST /api/subscriptions/{id}/terminate as CSR with no reason_code
Assert response status 422 with reason_code VALIDATION_ERROR

description: A subscriber-role principal calling POST /api/subscriptions/{id}/terminate receives HTTP 403.
steps: POST /api/subscriptions/{id}/terminate as a subscriber principal
Assert response status 403

description: Valid seeded staff credentials (CSR/ADMIN) return HTTP 200 with an access_token whose claims carry that role and subject.
steps: POST /api/auth/login with valid CSR/ADMIN credentials
Decode access_token
Assert role and subject claims match

description: A subscriber mobile number with no prior registration returns HTTP 200 with a pre-registration token (subscriber_id: null).
steps: POST /api/auth/login with an unregistered mobile_number
Assert response 200 with subscriber_id null

description: Invalid staff credentials (wrong password or unknown username) return HTTP 401 with the same generic UNAUTHENTICATED reason code in both cases (no user-enumeration signal).
steps: POST /api/auth/login with a wrong password for a known user
POST /api/auth/login with an unknown username
Assert both return 401 with identical reason_code and message shape

description: Exactly one seeded demo user exists for each of CSR, ADMIN, and DEALER roles after schema apply, with password_hash populated via a real hashing function, never plaintext.
steps: Apply schema
Query users table for each role
Assert exactly one row per role with a non-plaintext password_hash

description: A login attempt, successful or failed, never logs the raw password or an unmasked mobile number.
steps: Perform a successful login and a failed login
Capture emitted log lines
Assert no raw password appears and any mobile number is masked

description: A subscriber JWT issued by this endpoint for subscriber A is rejected with 403 when used against an endpoint scoped to subscriber B's data.
steps: Log in as subscriber A via the real endpoint
Call an endpoint scoped to subscriber B's data with A's token
Assert 403

description: A login page calls POST /api/auth/login and stores the returned token; registration/activation calls attach it as a bearer token.
steps: Load the login page
Submit valid credentials
Assert the token is stored and subsequent API calls include it as a bearer token

description: A role-based route guard redirects to the login page when no valid token is present, and blocks rendering a route scoped to a role the current token doesn't carry.
steps: Navigate to a protected route with no token
Assert redirect to login
Navigate to a route scoped to a different role's token
Assert the route is blocked
